what: Confidence of the first erroneous decision step for the baseline (117/218) and the final G-S configuration (191/218), on the same 218-item deep-chain exam, both from the gen36 factorial series. (a) ECDF of the top-1 operator probability at the first divergent step; (b,c) absolute-count histograms with a rug of the raw values.
one_line_reading: The final configuration does not make its remaining mistakes less confidently -- the ECDF shape is unchanged -- it makes far fewer of them: confidently-wrong decisions drop from 55 to 12.
method: p_max is read verbatim from chain.trace[k].p_max of the two persisted walk files at the first divergent decision step k (identical rule to gen36_erranalysis.py); nothing is re-estimated.
caveats: CORRECTION (an earlier analysis note suggested changing the section's 12 to 13 -- that suggestion is WITHDRAWN). The section's 12 comes from gen36/out/GEN36_WALK_gs.json, which is the SAME series as its baseline; under the single rule p_max>=0.9 that file gives exactly 12/27. Section 8 is self-consistent and needs no change. The earlier 13/27 came from pairing the gen35 baseline with a DIFFERENT checkpoint family (gen44 v7 s1, 220-op head).

Both readings coexist and are registered above: p_max>=0.9 gives 12/27 on the gen36 G-S walk and 13/27 on the gen44 s1 walk (27 errors in both). The single row that moves is ri=171 (p_max=0.9449, margin=0.8900). The four factorial arms reproduce Section 8's table exactly: errors 101/108/46/27 -> certified 117/110/172/191.
margin>=0.9 is NOT the section's rule; it is reported only for completeness (baseline 46/101, G-S 7/27). Do not mix the two.
This figure uses the gen36 in-series pair, so it is now directly citable by Section 8. The gen44 s1 re-test is the subject of fig_train_dynamics and fig_head_geometry instead.

The baseline walk is a different checkpoint (deep_plan_formal_6000) than the final one (deep_plan_formal_a2wt1_6000), but they belong to the same factorial series: same exam rows, same seed 20260923, same batch order md5.

'error' is defined as NOT (exact_hit and first_hit) on the operator chain, which reproduces the 101 / 27 counts exactly; it is a strict superset view of Lean certification, but on these files the two error sets coincide.

The ECDF shapes are almost indistinguishable; the effect in this comparison is in the COUNT of confidently-wrong decisions (55 -> 12), not in their probability distribution. A caption claiming better-calibrated errors would overreach.
